links.outcome: Readability (Flesch Kincaid Grade Level, Reading Ease) of ChatGPT-4 answers on retinal surgery
links.effect: Mean FKGL 14.1 (RD), 14 (MH), 14.8 (ERM); Flesch Reading Ease 32.3, 34.4, 28.1; difficult or very difficult, college graduation required.
links.quote: These scores indicate that the answers are difficult or very difficult to read for the average lay person and college graduation would be required to understand the material.

links.outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT-4 patient-directed answers relative to lay readers
links.effect: Average FKGL 14.1±2.6 (RD), 14±1.3 (MH), 14.8±1.3 (ERM); Reading Ease 28.1-34.4, above lay reading level.
links.quote: These scores indicate that the answers are difficult or very difficult to read for the average lay person and college graduation would be required to understand the material.

links.outcome: Appropriateness of ChatGPT-4 clinical answers on retinal surgery graded by retina specialists
links.effect: Consistently appropriate in 84.6% (33/39) RD, 92% (23/25) MH, 91.7% (22/24) ERM; inappropriate at least once in 5.1%, 8%, 8.3%.
links.quote: Responses were consistently appropriate in 84.6% (33/39), 92% (23/25), and 91.7% (22/24) of the questions related to RD, MH, and ERM, respectively.

screen.reason: Evaluates ChatGPT-4's appropriateness and readability for patient questions on vitreoretinal surgeries without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
